title: Pinecrest Advisory: annual model portfolio review
description: Legacy-name call for the 'improves over time' demo. Tom Alvarez, a principal advisor, refers to a fund by its former name, 'Contoso Heritage Compass Fund, Advisor class', which shares no vocabulary with the current catalogue, so it stays unresolved until a reviewer teaches the alias. Covers performance, taxes, model portfolios and materials, includes a harmless rapport fact (fly fishing) that should be kept, and has two dated seller tasks.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Hi Tom, it's Jordan. Can you see and hear me okay?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Hi, Jordan. Yes, loud and clear. Good to see you.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Likewise. Did you get out fishing at all before the cold set in?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Only a little, honestly. Mostly I've been tying flies at the kitchen table to get ready for my fly fishing trip to Montana in the spring.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: That sounds like the right way to spend a cold evening. All right, I know you wanted to go over your model review, so let's dig in.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Sure. As part of our annual review we're looking at everything in the models, and a number of our clients still hold the Contoso Heritage Compass Fund, Advisor class. I wanted to understand where it stands before we decide whether to keep it.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Makes sense. The Heritage Compass Fund is one of our longer-standing strategies, and a lot of advisors still call it by that name. Where would you like to start?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Performance first. How has the Heritage Compass Fund, Advisor class done against its benchmark over the last few years? A couple of my clients have been asking.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: It has outperformed its benchmark over the trailing three year and five year periods, though it did lag last quarter when the market was led by a narrow group of stocks.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: That's about what I expected. The other thing that comes up is taxes. Most of these clients hold it in taxable accounts, and last December some of them got hit with a big capital gains distribution.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: That's a fair concern. Distributions depend on realized gains and on how much money moves in and out during the year, and the numbers for this year are being finalized now.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Understood. Could you get me the figure as soon as it's available, so I can plan around it for the taxable clients?

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Absolutely. I'll email you the year-end distribution estimate by Tuesday.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Great. I'd also like to look at it against our models. We run a few model portfolios, and I'm thinking of keeping it as a satellite in the moderate and aggressive ones but dropping it from the conservative one.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: That's a reasonable approach. Keeping it as a satellite alongside your core holdings gives you diversification without letting it dominate the portfolio.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Right. Is there something current I can share with my team, like a one-pager for the Advisor class?

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Of course. I'll send you the current fact sheet and the trailing returns for the Advisor class tomorrow.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Perfect. I'll go through everything with my team on our side, and I'll let you know what we decide for the models.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Sounds great. Thanks for the time today, Tom, and good luck with the fly tying.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Thanks, Jordan. Talk soon.

surface_forms: Contoso Heritage Compass Fund, Advisor class

gold.notes: Legacy name of SYN-000021 (Contoso Growth Opportunities Fund Advisor Class). 'Heritage Compass' appears nowhere in the catalogue, so the system cannot resolve it until a reviewer teaches the alias; Tom states the Advisor class each time he names it. By design the script never uses equity, income, growth, bond, value, opportunities, dividend, global or international. Rapport fact to keep: Tom fly fishes (must_keep 'fishing'). For a Thursday call 'tomorrow' is 2026-11-20 and 'by Tuesday' is 2026-11-24. Tom going through everything with his team is a customer commitment, not a task.
